A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GenReward. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures and tables, are readable and support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original Meta-World experiments, policy comparisons, reward-component ablations, sensitivity analyses and generated-video-domain experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds results on distracting control, dexterous manipulation, component alternatives, hallucinated videos and computational cost.

M1.justification: v2 adds a text-to-video procedure without finetuning for DCS, whereas v1 describes finetuned image-to-video generation. This changes the generation inputs and adaptation procedure for that variant. The core video-level and forward-backward rewards, Algorithm 1 and Equations (1)–(10) remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained five Meta-World manipulation tasks, v2 evaluates DCS Walker Walk and Hopper Stand with background distractions, Adroit Door, and Meta-World Reach (Appendix A.2, Table A). This substantially extends task and environmental coverage beyond the earlier manipulation study.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain raw reward, RoboCLIP, Diffusion Reward and TADPoLe. New Tables C–D additionally evaluate a SigLIP 2 replacement and a real-video GenReward variant as comparators. These are limited comparator additions, rather than a replacement of the established baseline suite.

E3.justification: Appendix A.2 introduces evaluations using a DrQ-v2 implementation, dense rewards on DCS/Adroit, and limited-budget binary sparse rewards on Meta-World, reporting success rates for Adroit and Meta-World. New evaluations also measure FVD on 400 samples and training time over one million steps. The original DreamerV3 setup and hyperparameter table are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test hallucinated goal videos, random versus CLIP goal selection, DINOv3 versus SigLIP 2, removal of action information, and generated versus real videos (Tables B–D). Video-fidelity and runtime analyses are also added. The earlier reward-component ablations, sensitivity studies and CLIP failure case remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 10 episodes for the main comparison and display uncertainty bars. The added appendix tables use plus/minus reporting without establishing additional seeds, changed repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Under the retained stated main setup, Figure 5 revises Pick Out of Hole from 279/504 to 193/582 for raw reward/GenReward, and Shelf Place GenReward from 783 to 814. Sensitivity and domain curves, and the relocated sparse-reward baseline bar, also change. New Tables A–E add benchmark, robustness, component and runtime results; Appendix A.6 adds FVD 21.6.

T1.justification: The forward-backward appendix corrects the stated similarity quantity from F(s,a,z)^T B(s')ρ(ds') to F(s,a,z)^T B(s'). This is a local mathematical correction. The main equations and orthonormalization objective are retained, and no new proof or theorem is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the stated empirical effectiveness from Meta-World to Meta-World and Distracting Control Suite. The central contributions—generated video-level goals and action-aware forward-backward frame-level rewards—retain their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly acknowledges expert-data finetuning while describing a no-finetuning alternative, states that hallucinations are not addressed, and interprets the new results as showing retained utility despite hallucinations and competitiveness with real videos. The appendix also replaces mutual-reachability language with policy-conditioned future-state visitation. Existing computational and CLIP-selection limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 discloses seven days of video-model finetuning on 16 A100 GPUs and comparative training times. The detailed hyperparameter table and project link are retained. Conversely, the implementation paragraph drops the specific DINOv3-ViT-S/16+ identifier; this reduces documentation precision without establishing an actual model change.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for DCS, DeepMind Control, Adroit, DrQ-v2 and the forward-backward foundation by Touati et al., explicitly attributing the representation and loss derivation. Table 1 also changes VIPER's generative classification from no to yes. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: There are localized rewrites of implementation, analysis and related-work paragraphs, a renamed Section 3.1, and affiliation updates. The sparse-reward discussion moves into a new Additional Results appendix, with earlier appendix sections relabeled. Most narrative structure and wording remain intact.

P2.justification: New appendix Tables A–E substantially expand the quantitative presentation across benchmarks, robustness, components and runtime. The sparse-reward plot moves from main Figure 7 to appendix Figure A; the failure case and hyperparameter table become Figure B and Table F. Existing quantitative plots are redrawn with revised axes, while the method diagrams remain.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark and controlled experiments strengthen evidence about generality, component choices and generated-video reliability. Explicit forward-backward attribution and computational-cost disclosures improve transparency. However, the new experiments provide limited protocol detail, existing numerical revisions are unexplained, and the exact DINOv3 variant is no longer specified. These reporting limitations temper the supported overall improvement.
